items.stem: What is meant by “fragmentation”?
items.answer: Multiplication of an organism, such as a filamentous alga, by breaking of its body into pieces that grow into new individuals.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: multiplication of an organism, such as a filamentous alga, by breaking of its body into pieces that grow into new individuals.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about the characteristics of living organisms is correct?
items.answer: Mules and sterile worker bees do not reproduce, yet they are living.
items.markingKey: (c) Mules and sterile worker bees do not reproduce, yet they are living. The other statements are false. Reproduction cannot be all-inclusive: mules, sterile worker bees and infertile couples do not reproduce. Non-living objects such as mountains, boulders and sand mounds also grow by accumulation of material on the surface. In animals growth is seen only up to a certain age; in plants it continues throughout life.
options: Reproduction is a defining characteristic of all living organisms.
In animals, growth continues throughout life.
Mules and sterile worker bees do not reproduce, yet they are living.
Growth is a defining property of living organisms because non-living objects never increase in mass.

items.stem: The following statement is incorrect. Rewrite it correctly and give a reason: “Growth is a defining property of living organisms because non-living objects never increase in mass.”

items.markingKey: 1 mark for the corrected statement, 1 mark for the reason: Non-living objects such as mountains, boulders and sand mounds also grow by accumulation of material on the surface.

items.stem: “In unicellular organisms, growth and reproduction are synonymous.” Explain this statement.
items.answer: A unicellular organism such as a bacterium or Amoeba grows by cell division, and the same division produces new individuals; so an increase in number of cells is both growth and reproduction.
items.markingKey: 1 mark cell division as the means of growth; 1 mark the same division produces offspring; 1 mark example.

items.stem:

(iii) How would the observations differ if it were reproduction? Give two points. (2 marks)
items.answer: (i) Consciousness (ii) photoperiod affects flowering in plants (iii) absent in mules and sterile worker bees; may be asexual or sexual
items.markingKey: (i) consciousness – 1 mark. (ii) any one of: photoperiod affects flowering in plants – 1 mark. (iii) for reproduction: production of progeny similar to the parents; may be asexual or sexual; absent in mules and sterile worker bees – 1 mark each for any two.

items.stem: What are the characteristics of living organisms? Which of them are defining properties and which are not? Explain with examples.
items.answer: Growth – increase in mass and number; not defining as mountains, boulders and sand mounds also grow by accumulation. Reproduction – not defining as mules, sterile worker bees and infertile couples do not reproduce. Metabolism – sum of chemical reactions; defining as all organisms show it. Cellular organisation – defining. Consciousness – sensing and responding to the environment; defining; plants respond to photoperiod, humans show self-consciousness.
items.markingKey: 1 mark each for growth, reproduction, metabolism, cellular organisation and consciousness with the defining/non-defining reason.

items.stem: What is binomial nomenclature? State the rules for writing scientific names, with examples. Why is it needed?
items.answer: Naming with two components – generic name and specific epithet – given by Linnaeus. Rules: names in Latin or Latinised, written in italics; first word genus, second specific epithet; genus starts with a capital, epithet with a small letter; handwritten names underlined separately; author's name abbreviated after the epithet (Mangifera indica Linn.). Needed because local names vary and cause confusion; scientific names are universal and unique; codes ICBN and ICZN.
items.markingKey: 1 mark definition; 3 marks rules; 1 mark need.

items.stem: State any three universal rules of binomial nomenclature.
items.answer: Names are in Latin and written in italics; the first word is the genus and the second the specific epithet; the genus begins with a capital letter and the epithet with a small letter; handwritten names are underlined separately.
items.markingKey: 1 mark each for any three rules.

items.stem: Explain the term “family”.
items.answer: A group of related genera with still less number of similarities as compared to genus and species.

items.stem:
A student lists these points about one property of living organisms: increase in mass and number of cells; seen only up to a certain age in animals; occurs from inside in living organisms.
(i) Identify the property. (1 mark)
(ii) State one more feature you would expect to observe. (1 mark)
(iii) How would the observations differ if it were consciousness? Give two points. (2 marks)
items.answer: (i) Growth (ii) continues throughout life in plants (iii) ability to sense the environment; response to light, water, temperature and other stimuli
items.markingKey: (i) growth – 1 mark. (ii) any one of: continues throughout life in plants – 1 mark. (iii) for consciousness: ability to sense the environment; response to light, water, temperature and other stimuli; photoperiod affects flowering in plants – 1 mark each for any two.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about taxonomic categories and taxonomical aids is correct?
items.answer: As we go higher from species to kingdom, the number of common characteristics decreases.
items.markingKey: (b) As we go higher from species to kingdom, the number of common characteristics decreases. The other statements are false. Common characters decrease as we go higher in the hierarchy. A herbarium stores dried, pressed and preserved plant specimens on sheets; live plants are in botanical gardens. Both belong to family Felidae.
options: A herbarium is a place where live plants are grown for reference.
As we go higher from species to kingdom, the number of common characteristics decreases.
The number of common characters increases from species to kingdom.
Panthera and Felis are placed in different families.

items.stem: To which order does man belong?
items.answer: Primata
items.markingKey: (a) Man: order Primata.

items.stem: Distinguish between museum and botanical garden on any three points.
items.answer: Museum: preserved plant and animal specimens; larger animals may be stuffed; specimens kept in containers or jars in preservative solutions. Botanical garden: each plant labelled with scientific name and family; used for reference; collections of living plants.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for each of three correct, paired points of difference, e.g. museum – preserved plant and animal specimens; larger animals may be stuffed; specimens kept in containers or jars in preservative solutions; botanical garden – each plant labelled with scientific name and family; used for reference; collections of living plants.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about nomenclature and identification is correct?
items.answer: The name of the author is written after the specific epithet in abbreviated form, e.g. Mangifera indica Linn.
items.markingKey: (c) The name of the author is written after the specific epithet in abbreviated form, e.g. Mangifera indica Linn. The other statements are false. The genus starts with a capital letter; the specific epithet starts with a small letter. They are Latinised or derived from Latin and are the same all over the world. Carolus Linnaeus introduced it; Ernst Mayr is called the Darwin of the 20th century.
options: Scientific names are written in the local language of each country.
The specific epithet starts with a capital letter.
The name of the author is written after the specific epithet in abbreviated form, e.g. Mangifera indica Linn.

items.stem: Which term describes the sum total of all the chemical reactions occurring in the body of an organism?
items.answer: metabolism
items.markingKey: (a) Metabolism: the sum total of all the chemical reactions occurring in the body of an organism.

items.stem:
A taxonomical aid has these features: serves as a quick referral system; a store-house of plant specimens; sheets carry a label with name, family, collector and locality.
(i) Identify the taxonomical aid. (1 mark)
(ii) State one more feature you would expect to observe. (1 mark)
(iii) How would the observations differ if it were zoological park? Give two points. (2 marks)
items.answer: (i) Herbarium (ii) dried, pressed plant specimens on sheets (iii) help us learn food habits and behaviour; also called zoo
items.markingKey: (i) herbarium – 1 mark. (ii) any one of: dried, pressed plant specimens on sheets – 1 mark. (iii) for zoological park: wild animals kept in protected environments under human care; environments close to natural habitats; help us learn food habits and behaviour – 1 mark each for any two.

items.stem: A student lists these points about one property of living organisms: production of progeny similar to the parents; yeast and Hydra show budding; may be asexual or sexual. Identify the property. Give a reason.
items.answer: Reproduction
items.markingKey: 1 mark: reproduction; 1 mark: the features production of progeny similar to the parents; yeast and Hydra show budding; may be asexual or sexual are characteristic of it.

items.stem: Classify each of the following as taxonomical aid that preserves actual specimens or printed taxonomical aid: herbarium, museum, manual, zoological park.
items.answer: herbarium – taxonomical aid that preserves actual specimens; museum – taxonomical aid that preserves actual specimens; manual – printed taxonomical aid; zoological park – taxonomical aid that preserves actual specimens.
items.markingKey: ½ mark each: herbarium – taxonomical aid that preserves actual specimens; museum – taxonomical aid that preserves actual specimens; manual – printed taxonomical aid; zoological park – taxonomical aid that preserves actual specimens.

items.stem: Arrange the following in the correct classification of mango from kingdom to genus: Dicotyledonae, Angiospermae, Plantae, Sapindales. Give a reason.
items.answer: Plantae → Angiospermae → Dicotyledonae → Sapindales
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the order Plantae → Angiospermae → Dicotyledonae → Sapindales; 1 mark for the reason: NCERT Table 1.1.

items.stem: What is a taxonomic key? How is it used? Why are separate keys required?
items.answer: A taxonomical aid with contrasting characters in pairs (couplets); each statement is a lead; the user chooses one of two alternatives at each step until the organism is identified. Separate keys are needed for each category (family, genus, species).
items.markingKey: 1 mark each for definition, use, separate keys.

items.stem: Classify each of the following as generic name (genus) or specific epithet: Solanum, indica, Panthera, domestica.
items.answer: Solanum – generic name (genus); indica – specific epithet; Panthera – generic name (genus); domestica – specific epithet.
items.markingKey: ½ mark each: Solanum – generic name (genus); indica – specific epithet; Panthera – generic name (genus); domestica – specific epithet.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): ICBN provides rules for naming animals.
Reason (R): Each organism has only one valid scientific name.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: A is false, but R is true.
items.markingKey: (d) ICBN is for plants; ICZN for animals. R is true.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: Define the term “nomenclature”.
items.answer: The process of standardising the names of living organisms so that an organism is known by the same name all over the world.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: the process of standardising the names of living organisms so that an organism is known by the same name all over the world.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): In animals, growth continues throughout life.
Reason (R): Human beings are the only organisms known to be aware of themselves, i.e. to have self-consciousness.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: A is false, but R is true.
items.markingKey: (d) A is false: In animals growth is seen only up to a certain age; in plants it continues throughout life. R is a true statement.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem:
(a) Distinguish between zoological park and herbarium on any three points. (3 marks)
(b) A taxonomical aid has these features: dried, pressed plant specimens on sheets. Identify the taxonomical aid – zoological park or herbarium? Justify your answer. (2 marks)
items.answer: (a) Zoological park: wild animals kept in protected environments under human care; environments close to natural habitats; help us learn food habits and behaviour. Herbarium: dried, pressed plant specimens on sheets; sheets carry a label with name, family, collector and locality; serves as a quick referral system. (b) Herbarium.
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark for each of three paired differences. (b) 1 mark: herbarium; 1 mark: “dried, pressed plant specimens on sheets” is a feature of herbarium.

items.stem: The following statement is incorrect. Rewrite it correctly and give a reason: “In animals, growth continues throughout life.”
items.answer: In animals growth is seen only up to a certain age; in plants it continues throughout life.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the corrected statement, 1 mark for the reason: In animals growth is seen only up to a certain age; in plants it continues throughout life.

items.stem: Which of the following is a specific epithet?
items.answer: leo
items.markingKey: (a) Leo is a specific epithet; the others are not.

items.stem: A taxonomical aid has these features: preserved plant and animal specimens; specimens kept in containers or jars in preservative solutions. Identify the taxonomical aid.
items.answer: museum
items.markingKey: (c) Museum: preserved plant and animal specimens; specimens kept in containers or jars in preservative solutions.

items.stem: Define the term “species”.
items.answer: A group of individual organisms with fundamental similarities, the lowest taxonomic category.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: a group of individual organisms with fundamental similarities, the lowest taxonomic category.

items.stem:
A student lists these points about one property of living organisms: occurs from inside in living organisms; continues throughout life in plants; increase in mass and number of cells.
(i) Identify the property. (1 mark)
(ii) State one more feature you would expect to observe. (1 mark)
(iii) How would the observations differ if it were metabolism? Give two points. (2 marks)
items.answer: (i) Growth (ii) seen only up to a certain age in animals (iii) includes building up and breaking down of molecules; reactions can be demonstrated in vitro
items.markingKey: (i) growth – 1 mark. (ii) any one of: seen only up to a certain age in animals – 1 mark. (iii) for metabolism: sum of all chemical reactions in the body; shown by every living organism; reactions can be demonstrated in vitro – 1 mark each for any two.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about taxonomic categories and taxonomical aids is correct?
items.answer: Cat and dog are included in the same order, Carnivora, but in different families.
items.markingKey: (a) Cat and dog are included in the same order, Carnivora, but in different families. The other statements are false. Common characters decrease as we go higher in the hierarchy. A herbarium stores dried, pressed and preserved plant specimens on sheets; live plants are in botanical gardens. Both belong to family Felidae.
options: Cat and dog are included in the same order, Carnivora, but in different families.
The number of common characters increases from species to kingdom.
A herbarium is a place where live plants are grown for reference.
Panthera and Felis are placed in different families.

items.stem: To which family does wheat belong?
items.answer: Poaceae
items.markingKey: (a) Wheat: family Poaceae.
